dmp.description:
This Data Management Plan (DMP) has been developed for the project No. lzp-2023/1-0123, "Development of Biopolymer-based Hydrophobic Multi-layer Packaging Material from Biomass Waste Streams", funded by the Latvian Council of Science. The aim of the DMP is to outline the principles and procedures for managing the research data generated throughout the project. This includes data collection, documentation, storage, sharing, and long-term preservation. The DMP ensures compliance with FAIR data principles and promotes transparency, reproducibility, and the potential reuse of data. It will be updated as needed during the project to reflect any changes in data management practices.


1. Data Collection and Storage
All scientific results, datasets, and supporting materials created during the project  initially are stored in a secure Google Drive folder, accessible only to project team members. This workspace is used for collaborative work, version control, and interim data analysis.

2. Data Use and Access Control
Project data are primarily used for:

Preparing and submitting scientific publications,

Creating conference presentations and posters,

Internal analysis and reporting.

To protect the intellectual output of the research team, no data will be made publicly available before the corresponding research results are published in peer-reviewed articles. This is done to avoid premature disclosure or misuse by external researchers.

3. Data Sharing and Openness
After publication of the associated research:

The corresponding datasets and materials will be shared openly in a trusted repository (e.g., Zenodo), with a Digital Object Identifier (DOI) assigned, if necessary.

The shared data will be well-documented, following FAIR principles to ensure it is Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable.

In cases where ethical, legal, or privacy issues apply (e.g., personal data), data will be shared in anonymized form or under controlled access terms.

4. Data Security and Backup
During the active phase of the project:

Google Drive is used with institutional accounts to ensure compliance with security policies (e.g., encryption, access control).

Access is limited to authorized users with strong authentication.

Backups are managed by the cloud provider and reviewed periodically by the team.

5. Long-Term Preservation
After the project concludes:

Final datasets will be preserved in open repositories for at least 10 years.

Metadata and documentation will be included to support long-term reuse.

Project documentation will also be stored in institutional archives where possible.

6. Roles and Responsibilities
The Project Coordinator is responsible for overseeing data management. Designated team members are in charge of organizing, documenting, and uploading datasets after publication. No additional financial resources are required for data sharing, as the selected repositories are free and supported by the project institution.
